title: Which colour shows at each position of the signal?
description: A traffic signal repeats red, yellow, green, yellow. Dividing the position by four tells the colour, and expressions in n give the positions of red, yellow and green.
teaching_notes: One idea: the colours repeat every four positions, so the remainder after dividing by four decides the colour. Watch for students who forget that yellow comes twice in every cycle.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the matchstick steps: a pattern that repeats the same amount each time is written with the number of the step, here with n.
video_script.substitution: The method of the matchstick steps, where a formula is checked at a far step, with a colour cycle of four in place of two matchsticks.
video_script.anchor: a traffic signal that changes colour in a repeating order
video_script.payoff_line: Ninety and one hundred and ninety show yellow, and three hundred and forty three shows green

final_answer.value: 90 and 190 are yellow, 343 is green; red at 4n − 3, yellow at 2n, green at 4n − 1
final_answer.spoken: ninety and one hundred and ninety are yellow, three hundred and forty three is green; red is four n minus three, yellow is two n, green is four n minus one

hold_back: Answer: 90 and 190 are yellow, 343 is green; red at 4n − 3, yellow at 2n, green at 4n − 1
never_show: the colours at the far positions before their steps
maths_rules: cycle of 4: position 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 yellow, then repeats
remainder 1 red; remainder 2 or 0 yellow; remainder 3 green
90 = 4 x 22 + 2, so yellow; 190 = 4 x 47 + 2, so yellow; 343 = 4 x 85 + 3, so green
red at 4n - 3, yellow at 2n (every even position), green at 4n - 1
check: 343 = 4 x 86 - 1 is green; 90 = 2 x 45 and 190 = 2 x 95 are yellow
video_script.design: One idea: the colours repeat every four positions, so the remainder decides the colour. Assumes the example of a pattern that repeats. A strip of the first eight positions stays on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>A traffic signal changes colour in a repeating order.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>It goes red, yellow, green, yellow, and then red again.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>What colour shows at positions ninety, one hundred and ninety, and three hundred and forty three? Which positions show each colour?

beats.on_screen: the signal and the strip stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: positions 1 to 8 on a strip: red, yellow, green, yellow, red, yellow, green, yellow ; the order repeats every 4 positions

marks.g1: eight positions are coloured on a strip
marks.g2: a bracket marks each group of four positions

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>Number the colours one, two, three and so on along a strip.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The order repeats after every four positions.

beats.on_screen: Given: position 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 green, 4 yellow, then the order repeats

marks.gv1: the four colours are written against positions one to four

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, position one is red, two is yellow, three is green, and four is yellow. Then the order repeats.

beats.on_screen: To find: the colour at positions 90, 190 and 343 ; expressions for the positions of each colour
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We find the three colours, and then write the positions of each colour. We work the same way as the example in your book.

beats.on_screen: Step 1: divide the position by 4 ; remainder 1 is red ; remainder 2 or 0 is yellow ; remainder 3 is green

marks.s1b: the remainders are matched to the colours

narration: <bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, divide the position by four, and look at what is left.
<bookmark mark='s1b'/>Remainder one is red. Remainder two or zero is yellow. Remainder three is green.

marks.s2a: 90 is divided by 4 and the remainder 2 is marked
marks.s2b: 190 is divided by 4 and the remainder 2 is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, ninety divided by four leaves remainder two, so the signal is yellow.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>One hundred and ninety divided by four also leaves remainder two, so it is yellow too.

marks.s3a: 343 is divided by 4 and the remainder 3 is marked

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, three hundred and forty three divided by four leaves remainder three, so the signal is green.

beats.on_screen: Step 4: red at 4n − 3 ; yellow at 2n (every even position) ; green at 4n − 1
narration: <bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, red comes at one, five, nine and so on. These are four n minus three.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>Yellow comes at every even position, which is two n.
<bookmark mark='s4c'/>Green comes at three, seven, eleven and so on. These are four n minus one.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, check: 343 = 4 × 86 − 1 is green ; 90 = 2 × 45 and 190 = 2 × 95 are yellow

marks.s5a: 343 is written as 4n − 1 with n as 86

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Fifth, check with the expressions. Three hundred and forty three is four times eighty six minus one, so it is green.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>Ninety is two times forty five. One hundred and ninety is two times ninety five, so both are yellow.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 90 and 190 are yellow, 343 is green; red at 4n − 3, yellow at 2n, green at 4n − 1
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ninety and one hundred and ninety show yellow, and three hundred and forty three shows green.
<bookmark mark='ans2'/>Red is at four n minus three. Yellow is at two n. Green is at four n minus one.
